item.summary: Moments before an Air Canada plane collided with a ground vehicle at New York's LaGuardia Airport — killing two of its pilots — an air traffic controller is heard on the radio urgently telling the fire truck to stop and not cross the runway, using the word "stop" at least ten ...

item.title: How Major League Baseball players can turn to a robot to challenge balls, strikes this year
item.summary: Here's a brief explanation of how Major League Baseball will use technology this year to give players the opportunity to challenge calls on balls and strikes at the plate.

item.title: Jury finds Bill Cosby sexually assaulted woman in 1972, awards her nearly $60M US
item.summary: A civil jury in California found that Bill Cosby was liable for drugging and sexually assaulting a woman in 1972 and awarded her $59.25 million US on Monday.

item.title: Death toll rises to at least 33 in Colombian military plane crash
item.summary: A Colombian military transport plane with 121 people on board, mostly soldiers, crashed shortly after taking off Monday in Puerto Leguizamo, Colombia, killing at least 33 people and leaving at least 81 injured, according to the town's deputy mayor.

item.title: Kendra Duggar, wife of 19 Kids and Counting's Joseph Duggar, arrested
item.summary: Two days after the arrest of former 19 Kids and Counting star Joseph Duggar, an arrest warrant for his wife Kendra Duggar was also issued and served.

item.title: Turns out these sharks can make friends and have social lives, new study finds
item.summary: New research is suggesting that not all sharks are the lone, cold, ruthless predators as many films so often depict them. Some species, it turns out, can even be friendly — at least among their own kind.

item.title: U.S. Senate approves Markwayne Mullin as next head of Homeland Security
item.summary: The U.S. Senate confirmed Markwayne Mullin as homeland security secretary late Monday, approving President Donald Trump's nominee to take over the embattled department after the firing of Kristi Noem.

item.title: British police investigate burning of 4 ambulances belonging to Jewish charity
item.summary: Four ambulances belonging to a Jewish charity were set on fire early Monday in London in what British police are investigating as an antisemitic hate crime. Detectives are working to determine whether a claim of responsibility from a group with alleged links to Iran is authentic.
